title: "Electricity Export with HVDC"
completion: 100

## Architecture Definition

The electricity-export architecture carries electrical energy from each wind
turbine to the onshore electricity grid. Turbine output is conditioned for AC
infield collection, aggregated and converted to HVDC on an offshore platform,
exported to shore, and converted back to AC at the onshore grid connection.

The physical boundary includes the wind turbines, their support structures,
the complete offshore and onshore electrical chain, and the grid-connection
interface. It ends where the project hands electrical energy to the onshore
grid.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-height: 1.0
flowchart LR
  A["Wind turbine"] --> B["Turbine electrical conversion"]
  B --> C["AC infield collection"]
  C --> D["Offshore AC aggregation and HVDC conversion"]
  D --> E["HVDC export"]
  E --> F["Onshore conversion"]
  F --> G["Electricity-grid connection"]
```

## Included Physical Functions

| Function | Treatment | Canonical owner |
|---|---|---|
| Wind-energy capture and generation | Included | [Wind Turbine](../turbine_system/wind_turbine.qmd) |
| Turbine support structure | Included | [Foundation](../turbine_system/foundation.qmd) |
| Turbine rectification, inversion, and transformation | Included | [Wind Turbine Mass and Cost](../turbine_system/wind_turbine.qmd) |
| AC infield collection | Included | [Infield AC Cables](../electrical_infra/infield_ac_cables.qmd) |
| Offshore AC aggregation and HVDC conversion | Included on the electricity-export platform function | [HVDC Converter Stations](../electrical_infra/hvdc_converter_stations.qmd) |
| Offshore platform structure | Included | [Platform Material CAPEX](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd) |
| HVDC export to shore | Included | [HVDC Export Cables](../electrical_infra/hvdc_export_cables.qmd) |
| Onshore conversion and project connection interface | Included | [Onshore Grid Connection](../electrical_infra/onshore_grid_connection.qmd) |

Cable, platform, turbine, and foundation installation are within the economic
boundary. Their methods and assumptions are maintained in the
[Offshore Installation](../offshore_installation/overview.qmd) section rather
than repeated here.

## Excluded Functions

The following functions are outside this architecture:

- offshore hydrogen production and water treatment
- hydrogen compression
- hydrogen infield and export pipelines
- electricity-network infrastructure beyond the defined onshore connection
- downstream electricity storage, distribution, and end use

## Architecture Interfaces

| Interface | Boundary definition |
|---|---|
| Turbine to infield network | Electrical output passes through the turbine conversion chain into the AC collection network. |
| Infield network to offshore platform | AC feeders terminate at the offshore collection and conversion platform. |
| Offshore platform to export system | Converted DC power enters the HVDC cable system. |
| Export system to onshore connection | The onshore converter returns the exported power to AC for handover at the grid connection. |

## Economic Boundary

The architecture cost includes the common offshore wind project and all
electricity-specific assets and lifecycle activities needed to reach the
onshore grid connection. Common turbine, foundation, development, and financing
costs remain part of the comparison even though they also apply to the hydrogen
architectures.

Wider onshore grid reinforcement is outside the base architecture boundary
unless it is explicitly assigned to the project by the scenario. Costs,
losses, availability, sizing, and unresolved evidence remain owned by the
linked component and methodology pages.
